name: locker.github/catalog
title: GitHub.Locker
description: Find open-source GitHub projects by task, see trending repos and read plain-language summaries.

tools.name: search_projects
tools.description: Find open-source GitHub projects in the GitHub.Locker catalog by what they do. Use it when the user describes a need or a kind of tool ("a self-hosted alternative to Notion", "a Rust terminal"), and with sort week or month for what is rising within that topic. Every word of the query must appear in the project's name, description, summary, topics or language, so pass short keywords. Returns projects with stars, recent star gains, a one-line summary and links. For what is trending on GitHub overall use trending_projects; for details on one repository use get_project.

query.description: One or two short keywords per idea; every word must appear in the project.

language.description: Only projects whose main language is this, case-insensitive.

sort.description: stars: most-starred first; day, week or month: most stars gained in that period first.

tools.name: trending_projects
tools.description: The GitHub projects that gained the most stars on the last closed GitHub day, or over the last week or month, from GitHub.Locker's daily ranking. Use it when the user asks what is trending, hot or new on GitHub without naming a topic. For trending projects within a topic use search_projects with sort week or month instead.

period.description: day: the last closed GitHub day (Pacific time); week: the last 7 days; month: the last 30 days.

limit.description: How many projects to return, highest gain first.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: One project from the GitHub.Locker catalog as markdown: what it is, questions and answers about it (platforms, install, pricing, privacy), stars, language and license, similar projects, its topics and the start of its README. Use it when the user names a specific repository or link, or to check a project from search_projects or trending_projects before recommending it. To find projects you do not know yet use search_projects.

project.description: owner/repo, or a github.com or github.locker link to the project.
